title: Architecture-aware microkernel selection policy for mixed-length token pipelines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight, bankable policy layer that picks the optimal microkernel implementation at request time based on (1) hardware fingerprint (GPU arch + compute capability), (2) live sequence-length distribution, and (3) pipeline phase (prefill vs decode). This ticket delivers the policy, a small online profiler, and a canary rollout path integrated with the runtime router.
acceptance_criteria: Policy selects non-default microkernel for >=10% of requests in canary workload when it reduces per-token latency by >=8%
End-to-end regression tests for prefills and decodes pass across Ampere/Turing/Intel accelerators in CI
Online profiler has <2ms median overhead for cold-starts and <0.2ms overhead for warm requests
Console dashboard shows kernel-choice breakdown by region, model, and seqlen bucket
Canary rollout supports A/B and automatic rollback based on p50 latency and error-rate SLOs
technical_notes: We treat kernel implementations as orthogonal variants referenced by unique kernel IDs. The policy is a small decision tree + lightweight cost-model; not a heavy bandit controller to keep predictability.
Hardware fingerprint will be derived from device PCI ID + driver version + available shared memory; map maintained in /etc/redwood/kernel-profiles and synced from model-onboarding service.
SeqLen buckets: {short: <=32, mid: 33-256, long: >256}. Prefill vs decode phases are annotated on request context already in the runtime path.

Online profiler probes a very small set of representative ops (attention forward + KV cache write) for ~50 prefill requests per device during low-load windows to update estimates. Profiling is rate-limited and persisted as time-series metrics.
Cost model uses smoothed per-token microsecond estimates with per-arch priors and a tiny regularizer to avoid thrashing between kernels.
We will surface suggested quantization/kernel pairings from Optimize team as optional hints; policy must ignore hints if they violate compatibility rules.
Compatibility matrix for kernels must be consulted before selecting (e.g., some kernels incompatible with fused rotary or with certain quantized weights).
implementation_plan: Spec: finalize policy decision graph and profiling rules (documented in Confluence: /confluence/runtime/kernel-policy) - 2d
Proto: implement in runtime as KernelPolicy module with pluggable backends - 4d
Profiler: lightweight probe task + persistence to metrics - 3d
CI: add arch-sim tests and microbench harnesses for Ampere/Turing/Intel - 3d
Console: small dashboard work to visualize kernel choices and perf deltas - 3d
Rollout: canary config and rollback hooks; run internal canary for two clusters - 4d

comments: 2026-02-11 Maya Chen: Initial spike showed that short sequences on Turing benefit most from tiled-attention kernel A vs default by ~12% p50 token latency.
2026-02-20 Luis Alvarez: Updated decision tree to require minimum observed improvement of 5% and 1k sample history before switching kernels to reduce oscillation.
2026-02-27 QA (Rohit Patel): Found a correctness edge-case when rotary embeddings are fused and kernel B is chosen; added compatibility check in the policy.
2026-03-01 SRE (Aisha Gomez): Profiling probes caused a minor spike in device clocking on one node during initial rollout; we throttled probes to 1/minute per device and issue resolved.
2026-03-04 Product (Elena Ford): Requesting console view grouped by customer tier and model to assess economic impact for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-05 Luis Alvarez: Prototype merged to staging (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2109). Running automated perf suites against Ampere and Intel nodes. Next: schedule internal canary next week.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the compatibility matrix and the profiler throttling logic.
We intentionally keep the policy conservative (require warm-history and minimum improvement) to avoid degrading tail latency under noisy workloads.
postmortem_plan: If canary shows >1% increase in p99 or >0.5% change in error rate, trigger rollback and collect device traces + kernel-level counters for 24 hours for root cause analysis.
observability_goals: Expose kernel_choice, kernel_latency_us, profile_samples_count, and cache_hit_rate to per-tenant metrics. Track cost_delta_us_per_token for economic dashboard.
estimated_savings: Expected 6-12% per-token compute savings for mixed workloads with heavy short-mid sequence traffic (based on internal benchmarks).
